report.summary: Chunk 1 of 2: defines data structures (ForestNode, ForestEdge, ForestHyperedge, KnowledgeForest) and helper functions for building a knowledge forest snapshot from an index dict.
risks: _is_type_node_id | medium | The function checks for '#' separator but the docstring claims 'no path in an indexed repo carries' it. If a repo path contains '#', it could be misclassified. To settle: check if any indexed repo path can contain '#' (unlikely but possible on some filesystems).

KnowledgeForest.content_sha256 | low | Uses json.dumps with sort_keys=True, but dict ordering in Python 3.7+ is insertion-order; sort_keys ensures determinism. However, to_dict returns a dict with keys in a fixed order; sorting is redundant but safe.

build_knowledge_forest | medium | The function signature includes temporal_pairs but the chunk ends before processing it. The docstring claims 'Missing or out-of-scope members are skipped' but no code is shown to verify that behavior.

handoff.purpose: Define data structures and helper functions for building a deterministic knowledge forest snapshot.

symbols.name: SCHEMA_VERSION
symbols.note: String constant 'daedalus-forest/1' used as default schema version.

symbols.name: _json_value
symbols.note: Recursively converts a value to a deterministic JSON-compatible form, sorting mappings by key and sorting sets/lists.

symbols.name: ForestNode
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with id, kind, attributes. Has to_dict method.

symbols.name: ForestEdge
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with source, target, relation, directed, weight, evidence, attributes. Has to_dict method.

symbols.name: ForestHyperedge
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with id, relation, members, weight, evidence, attributes. Has to_dict method.

symbols.name: KnowledgeForest
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing a deterministic evidence snapshot. Contains root, nodes, edges, hyperedges, provenance, schema. Has to_dict, content_sha256, layer_counts.

symbols.name: _CLONE_RELATIONS
symbols.note: Mapping from index keys to relation names for clone clusters.

symbols.name: _TYPE_NODE_KINDS
symbols.note: Frozenset of node kinds that are not files: 'type' and 'field'.

symbols.name: _RESERVED_RELATIONS
symbols.note: Frozenset of relation names that are reserved for specific layers.

symbols.name: _canonical_key
symbols.note: Returns a deterministic JSON string key for sorting attribute mappings.

symbols.name: _is_type_node_id
symbols.note: Returns True if node_id starts with 'type:' or 'field:' and contains '#'.

symbols.name: _hyperedge_id
symbols.note: Generates a deterministic hyperedge ID from relation, members, and cluster data.

symbols.name: _clone_members
symbols.note: Extracts sorted member identifiers from a cluster mapping.

symbols.name: build_knowledge_forest
symbols.note: Normalizes an index dict and optional temporal pairs into a KnowledgeForest. Chunk ends partway through.

claims.text: The 'forest' is a product metaphor, not a claim that software is an acyclic tree.
claims.why: The module name 'forest' is used metaphorically; no code asserts acyclicity.

claims.text: A repository contains cycles, relations with different meanings, and groups that cannot be represented faithfully as pairwise edges.
claims.why: The module defines hyperedges (ForestHyperedge) to handle groups, and edges with different relations (ForestEdge.relation).

claims.text: nodes are indexed source files, and -- when the index carries them -- DOCUMENTS and TYPES/FIELDS, which are the same contract with a different ``kind``;
claims.why: The code defines ForestNode with a 'kind' field, but does not specify which kinds are indexed. The index contents are not shown.

claims.text: edge layers keep imports, document links, type structure and temporal co-change evidence separate;
claims.why: The code defines edges with a 'relation' field, but does not show how layers are separated. The _RESERVED_RELATIONS constant hints at some layers, but actual separation logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: hyperedge preserve clone groups without expanding them into fake cliques.
claims.why: The module defines ForestHyperedge class to represent groups directly, and _CLONE_RELATIONS maps cluster types to hyperedge relations.

claims.text: Symbols, build targets, schemas, runtime spans, and domain entities can be added as new node kinds and relation layers without changing this contract -- ``document`` (node kind) and ``documents`` (relation layer) were added exactly that way, and ``type``/``field`` were added the same way again, and all three cost this file no new field, no new dataclass and no schema bump.
claims.why: The code shows generic dataclasses (ForestNode, ForestEdge) that can accommodate new kinds/relations, but the claim about specific additions (document, type, field) and no schema bump is not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: No latent coordinates or partitions are inferred here. The snapshot is evidence-preserving input for later, independently evaluated algorithms.
claims.why: The functions in this chunk are purely structural; they do not perform inference or coordinate assignment.

claims.text: ``document`` joined ``dss.FILE_NODE_KINDS``; ``type`` and ``field`` deliberately did NOT, and a future reader must not 'finish the job' by adding them.
claims.why: The code defines _TYPE_NODE_KINDS as {'type', 'field'} and comments that they are not in FILE_NODE_KINDS, but the actual FILE_NODE_KINDS set is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: A document has BYTES ON DISK. It can be a hierarchy leaf, a selection seed and a candidate for a token budget, because ``n_tokens`` is a measurement of it.
claims.why: The code does not define 'document' or 'n_tokens'; these are external concepts.

claims.text: A ``type`` node is a DERIVED assertion about a region of a file that is already a node in its own right; it has no bytes of its own.
claims.why: The code does not define type nodes beyond the _TYPE_NODE_KINDS constant; no behavior is shown.

claims.text: Pack it and ``dss._estimated_tokens`` falls through to its ``loc * 8`` fallback and invents a cost for something that cannot be read into a prompt
claims.why: dss._estimated_tokens is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The same asymmetry holds for the safety fence. ``graph.fenced_dominance`` divides by ``graph._graph_nodes``, which is fed by ``index['modules']`` and ``index['import_edges']``.
claims.why: graph.fenced_dominance and graph._graph_nodes are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Type nodes have no forward imports, so every one of them would land in the denominator and none in the numerator: ``fraction`` falls, ``provider_router``'s reachability stand-down stops firing, and every task stays on the premium lane.
claims.why: provider_router and stand-down logic are not in this chunk.

claims.text: the type layer lives in ``type_nodes``/``type_edges`` and never in ``modules`` or ``import_edges``.
claims.why: The code shows module_ids derived from index['modules'] but does not show type_nodes/type_edges handling.

claims.text: This file honours that by keeping ``module_ids`` (the membership gate of four other layers) closed to them.
claims.why: module_ids is defined as {str(module) for module in modules} from index['modules']; no type nodes are added to it.

claims.text: And the type relations are a LENS, not a diffusion channel. The fan-in of ``Path``/``dict``/``str`` in this repo was MEASURED before the layer was built: uncapped, 'two functions that mention the same type are two hops apart' makes 53.6% of all function pairs adjacent, i.e. the graph is effectively complete.
claims.why: No measurement or fan-in data is present in this chunk; the claim refers to external analysis.

claims.text: So ``dss._relation_adjacencies`` filters diffusion to file-kind endpoints; these layers are published for consumers that ask about them by name, and the hub cap that would make them diffusible is measured and reported in ``index['types']['coverage']``, not assumed.
claims.why: dss._relation_adjacencies and index['types']['coverage'] are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The 'kind:' prefix follows the 'repo:'/'dir:'/'file:' convention already used by ``dss``'s derived hierarchy, and the '#' separator is a character no path in an indexed repo carries
claims.why: The claim about '#' not appearing in repo paths is not verifiable from this code; it depends on the repository's file naming conventions.

claims.text: ``build_forest_hierarchy`` segments node ids on '/' and would otherwise happily read 'type:pkg/mod.py#Foo' as the directory 'type:pkg'.
claims.why: build_forest_hierarchy is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The kind filter is what actually keeps a type node out of the file world; this is defence in depth, and it makes a leak legible in a diff instead of only in a stack trace.
claims.why: The function _is_type_node_id explicitly checks for 'type:' or 'field:' prefix and '#' separator, acting as a filter.

claims.text: ``temporal_pairs`` should use ``structcore.churn.co_change_pairs`` rows.
claims.why: structcore.churn.co_change_pairs is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Missing or out-of-scope members are skipped instead of manufacturing nodes.
claims.why: The function body is incomplete; the processing logic is not shown.

claims.text: Negative/zero PMI evidence is kept only in attributes; the non-negative edge weight is the pair's lift, which has the intuitive neutral value 1.
claims.why: No PMI or edge weight handling is shown in this chunk.

observations.what: The docstring makes many claims about external modules and behavior not present in this chunk.
_is_type_node_id uses a heuristic (presence of '#') that may not be foolproof if a repo path contains '#'.
The chunk ends abruptly in the middle of build_knowledge_forest; the function is incomplete.
